data.name: Adiman
data.gender_notes: Adiman is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Adiman is a Sanskrit name derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Adi’ which means ‘first’ or ‘beginning’. The suffix ‘man’ denotes ‘man’ or ‘god’. Thus, Adiman signifies the primeval being, the first god in Hindu mythology. The name Adiman carries the meaning “First God, Primeval Being” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Adiman usually hope their child will grow to embody first god, primeval being and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of creation, the embodiment of the divine and the source of all existence.

data.cultural_impact: Adiman holds a significant place in Hindu mythology, particularly in the Shiva Purana and Bhagavata Purana. It is believed that Adiman is the primal deity, the first creation of the universe by Brahma. He is also referred to as Adishesha, the first serpent who lies below Vishnu in the cosmic ocean, supporting the universe. The name Adiman is a reminder of the formidable roots and rich cultural history of Hinduism.
data.spiritual_significance: Adiman is considered as the ancestor of all deities in Hinduism, and thus holds immense spiritual significance. In Hindu philosophy, Adiman is depicted as the primeval consciousness, the ultimate reality, the source of all existence. Moreover, Adiman is believed to be beyond time, space, and causation, an eternal and unchanging reality. To devotees of Adiman, he represents the ultimate goal of spiritual realization, the attainment of Brahman or the absolute truth. The name Adiman serves as a reminder of the infinite potential within oneself and the sacredness of life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Adiman signifies the primal, original being, the first cause or creator. It embodies the eternal and infinite essence of consciousness and knowledge, representing the divine source of all existence.

historical_references.reference: The Puranas mention Adiman as a manifestation of the supreme deity Vishnu, representing his eternal and unchanging aspect. Adiman is often depicted as the first embodiment of the universe, the unmanifested and infinite cosmic ocean.
historical_references.time_period: Ancient India, circa 4th century BCE to 12th century CE

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Adiman can be found in the Mahabharata, where he is described as the original form of Shiva, the destroyer god, before he assumed his more common form as Rudra. Adiman is said to represent the state of pure consciousness or Turiya, beyond the waking, dreaming, and deep sleep states of consciousness.
